question: For a number of years, animal welfare associations have been speaking out in the media about the mistreatment of Spanish greyhounds. Reared for hunting, these greyhounds are often mistreated, locked up in poor conditions, and then abandoned as soon as they are no longer useful. At the end of the season, the least effective dogs may be subjected to violence, abandoned or be put down.
Despite the work of grassroots associations, the structural problem remains: as long as hunting with greyhounds is allowed, these abuses and acts of cruelty will continue. 1.
What specific action can the EU executive take as part of its pet welfare strategy (dogs and cats)?
Does the Commission intend to take action to improve the protection of greyhounds used for hunting, in particular to protect them against being abandoned, ill-treated and put down?
